input:
This executive summary reviews the delivery performance of a contract packaging firm that operates 2 plants and generates revenue of $60 million per year. The analysis is based on order records for 12 months, covering a total of 15726 orders, and focuses in particular on the last two quarters, during which on-time delivery was 91%, compared with a target of 95%.

A number of concerning trends can be identified. Overtime cost reached $2.5 million last year, which represents an increase of 29% compared with the year before, while the order backlog has grown to 3.8 weeks, up from just 1.7 weeks a year ago. It is also notable that Plant 2 is responsible for 59% of late orders, suggesting that Plant 2 is where the problem is concentrated rather than evenly spread across the business. A scheduling system covering all plants has been quoted at $334k, while Plant 2 alone would cost $129k. According to an internal estimate, which it should be stressed is not a vendor figure, installing the system at Plant 2 could reduce overtime at Plant 2 by 15-20% in the first year.

In light of these findings, the recommendation under consideration is to install the system at Plant 2 first, at $129k, while holding the other plants until results from Plant 2 are reported, rather than committing the full $334k at once. The scheduling programme is owned by the operations director, who will oversee Plant 2's implementation and the wider programme going forward.
